title: Amphenol (APH)
headline: Amphenol: the data-center pick I’m betting on heavily
standfirst: Amphenol makes the connectors, antennas and sensors packed into modern data centers — and the returns are, frankly, ridiculous. It’s one of the highest grades I’ve ever given. My grade: 8.6–9.1.
author: Daniel Reynolds
summary: Amphenol (APH) sells the connectors and sensors that fill modern data centers — Strong Buy on the Street, exceptional returns, and one of my highest grades ever (8.6–9.1).

blocks.md: Amphenol is a critical manufacturer and parts distributor that makes serious money selling **connectors, antennas, sensors** and related gear — the kind of stuff packed into modern data centers by the ton. And it’s getting some real love from analysts: it’s rated a **Strong Buy** on the Street. So let’s dive in.

blocks.label: My grade
blocks.md: **8.6 – 9.1.** This lands in the **top 1%** of stocks I’ve ever graded, and I’m betting on it heavily. It’s well-rounded, it’s growing fast, and — for a company this size and quality — I honestly can’t find a good reason it isn’t *more* expensive.

blocks.text: Doing really well — and not expensive for it

blocks.md: To be honest, I’d never heard of it before — and it’s absolutely shooting up. It sits near its peak price from a few days ago, but it still isn’t *expensive* for what you get. It just released a dividend of about **$0.125** a quarter, and out of all the multi-billion-dollar companies in this space, the price is ridiculously reasonable. Through 2024 it added just over **$2 billion** in earnings, and it’s been beating its earnings by good amounts. The latest professional rating? A **Strong Buy** (18 analysts), with an average target around **$99.39** — roughly 18% above today’s ~$84.
This is the part that got my attention. The return rates are ridiculous — this is why it’s in my top 1%.

blocks.title: Total return (my own figures — unverified)
blocks.sub: Most of the five-year gain came in the last three. See the caveat below before trusting these.
blocks.source: ⚠️ These three figures come from my own research notes and I could NOT independently verify them against a primary source, so treat them as indicative rather than confirmed. What I can verify: Amphenol's 2025 revenue rose ~52% to $23.1B and earnings ~76% to $4.27B. Past performance is never a forecast.

blocks.md: Amphenol is the classic picks-and-shovels play: it doesn’t matter which data-center or AI company wins, they *all* need connectors and sensors, and Amphenol sells them across communications, harsh-environment, and interconnect/sensor segments. Revenue and earnings are both growing fast, the Street is on board, and the price still isn’t stretched for the quality. It’s well-rounded — and I truly can’t find a reason it’s not more expensive. I’m definitely going to recommend this one.

items.title: It’s priced for growth.
items.body: A ~42 P/E means the market already expects a lot. If growth slows, a stock this loved can re-rate quickly.

items.title: A run this big can’t repeat forever.
items.body: +313% over three years is spectacular — and exactly the kind of number that doesn’t simply continue. I’m sizing with that in mind.

items.title: It rides the AI cycle.
items.body: So much demand now comes from data centers; a pause in the AI build-out would hit orders.

blocks.heading: One of my highest grades — and a heavy bet
blocks.md: Amphenol is well-rounded, fast-growing, Strong-Buy-rated, and *still* not expensive for the quality. It’s a top-1% grade for me and one I’m betting on heavily. **My grade: 8.6–9.1.** The only caution is the obvious one: after a run like this, respect the risk and don’t assume the last three years repeat.

disclaimer: Independent, educational research and my own opinions — not investment advice. My grade is my own judgment, not a prediction of returns; the total-return figures are from my research and past performance does not predict the future. Figures as of Sep 29, 2026 — verify and do your own research.
